HM Borhan, Advocate------ For the Petitioner.

parties:
Kazi Rashed Akhter Shahid (Prince) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Rokshana Choudhury (Sanda) ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of defendant- appellant petitioner is directed against the judgment and decree dated 16-2-2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Tangail in Family Appeal No. 37 of 2002 affirming the judgment and decree dated 17-10-2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge and Family Judge, Sadar Tangail in Family Case No. 11 of 1999 decreeing the case. 

 6. The defendant-petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 57 of 1999 under Order XLVII, rules 1 and 2 on 8-6-1999. The Miscellaneous case was allowed on 7-7-1999 and the case was restored to its original file and number. Again, due to nonappearance of the defendant, the suit was fixed for ex parte hearing on 17-10-2002. 

 8. The learned Assistant Judge and Family Judge, Sadar Tangail on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record decreed the suit ex parte on 17-10-2002 allowing the prayer for restoration of conjugal right granting dower of Taka 1,50,000 and maintenance of Taka 55,000. 

 11. Mr HM Borhan, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the learned District Judge, Tangail passed the judgment and decree without going deep into the facts and circumstances of the case and the laws applicable thereto; that the judgment and decree passed by the learned District Judge, Tangail is slipshod and did not reveal the facts and legal consequences involved in the case; that the learned District Judge Tangail did not consider the Talaq given by the defendant petitioner to the plaintiff-opposite party in its true and legal perspective, that the learned District Judge, did not consider the social and economic position of the defendant-petitioner nor enquired about the income of the petitioner and that the learned District Judge ought to have seen that dower amount of the marriage, if any, according to her status cannot be more than 30,000 (thirty thousand). He further submits that the judgment and decree passed by the learned lower Court are neither proper nor in accordance with law and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree caused serious injury to the petitioner occasioning failure of justice. 

 12. The learned Advocate for the petitioner referred the case of Serajul Islam vs Helana Begum and others reported in 48 DLR 48 in support of his contention. 

 14. Mr Abul Quashem further submits that on receipt of summons the defendant contested the said family suit by filing written statement denying the case of the plaintiff alleging, inter alia, that the Kabinnama was the product of forgery. Thereafter several dates for pre emptory hearing were fixed but the contesting defendant failed to attend the Court nor did take any step on any of the dates of hearing and thus the trial Court decreed the suit against the defendant considering the facts of the case and evidence on record by his judgment and decree dated 17-2-2002. 

 24. In the instant case the petitioner has totally failed to prove by any convincing  evidence that the notice of talaq was sent to the chairman and a copy thereof to the opposite party. A talaq will not be effective even after the expiry of 90 days if any of the conditions of effectiveness of talaq i.e. pronouncement as per Mohammedan Law, service of notice on chairman and a copy thereof to wife is not complied with. The chairman, on receipt of notice addressed to him by the husband, shall constitute an arbitration council headed by him to reconcile the parties. The arbitration council so constituted will be represented by each of the parties by their respective representatives. A reference may be made to the case of PLD(1975) Lah. 466. 

 25. In the instant case, the petitioner has totally failed to prove that the chairman received such notice. Since it has not been proved that the petitioner issued the notice of talaq to the Chairman, then the constitution of arbitration council to reconcile the parties does not arise. 

 26. Mr Abul Quashem, the learned Advocate, cited the decision in the case of Shajiqul Islam and others vs State reported in 46 DLR 700 wherein their Lordships decided that a divorce under the Ordinance is not a unilateral act, rather it involves a public authority in the matter. It precludes a divorce or talaq from being effective for a period of ninety days from the date of the receipt of the notice by the Chairman. Consequently, the marital status of the parties will not in any way change during that period. The parties in law will continue to remain husband and wife till the divorce is confirmed. In the instant case the petitioner has totally failed to prove that the notice upon the chairman was served and that the Chairman constituted an arbitration council to reconcile the matter. 

 28. In the instant case it appears that defendant Kazi Rashed Akhter Shahid (prince) married the plaintiff by registered kabinnama on 11-1-1996; that at the instigation of his parents he left the plaintiff Most Rokshana Choudhury (Sanda) at the house of her father since 28-3-1998 uncared for and did not pay a single farthing towards her maintenance; the petitioner did neither try to bring her nor did he maintain his wife. It is fully an unkind attitude of the petitioner towards his wife. The Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 is a beneficial legislation. The object of the provision of this Ordinance is certainly for the benefit of the vast majority of a particular class of people. From the reading of section 7 of the said Ordinance the object of the said section is to give a benefit to the female preventing a hasty dissolution of marriage by talaq being pronounced by the husband unilaterally without giving any scope for reconsideration but such benevolent intention is likely to be converted into an instrument of abuse and tyranny by the husband instead of preventing the said abuse may aggravate the suffering without end. On plain reading of section 7 of the Ordinance 1961, it can be said that it was never the intention of the legislature that a husband exercising his independent act pronouncing talaq cannot be given effect to until and unless such notice is given to the chairman and it means if a husband divorces his wife but does not give notice purposely to the chairman then the divorce will not be effective till eternity. The intention of the legislature while enacting the said Ordinance 1961 was to prevent hasty dissolution of marriage and a duty is cast upon the husband to give notice under section 7 of the said Ordinance. If he failed to do so intentionally the very object of the said section becomes redundant. In this case, the petitioner at the instigation of his parents, left his wife at the house of her father at Tangail since 28-3-1998 uncared for and did not pay a single farthing towards her maintenance. It further appears that the petitioner contested the suit but he adopted dilatory tactics to harass the opposite party. It shows that he purposely avoided to give notice to the Chairman of Tangail Municipality, so question of reconciling was not held. All these unfair activities of the petitioner made her life miserable. 

 32. In the instant case, the plaintiff Most. Rokshana Choudhury (Sanda) as PW 1 deposed that the, petitioner, at the instigation of his parents, left her in her father's house at Tangail since 28-3-1998 uncared for and did not pay a single farthing towards her maintenance. The petitioner has totally failed. to show any evidence to the effect that he gave any maintenance to his wife. 

 36. Considering the aforesaid statutory provisions and in view of above decisions cited above, we do not find any reason to hold otherwise. Accordingly, it is held that the Court has the jurisdiction to pass a decree for past maintenance in an appropriate case like the instant one and the Court below has committed no illegality in passing the decree for maintenance for plaintiff-opposite party. 

 37. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred the case of Serajul Islam vs Helana Begum and others reported in 48 DLR 48 in support of his contention. In our case under review since it has been proved that the service of notice upon the Chairman and other requirement of law were not at all proved and thus the marriage subsists. So, the facts and circumstances of the cited case of the petitioner are quite distinguishable from the present case, as such, cited cases are of no assistance of the petitioner. 

 38. In the facts of the case we have no hesitation to form opinion that the appellate Court rightly applied his judicial mind and passed the impugned judgment and decree dated 16-2-2004.in Family Appeal No. 37 of 2002 affirming the judgment and decree dated 17-10-2002 passed by the learned Senior Assistant. Judge and Family Judge, Sadar Tangail in Family Suit No. 11 of 1999. He passed the impugned judgment and decree assigning genuine reasons. We do not find any illegality and legal infirmity in the impugned judgment and decree occasioning failure of justice to justify interference by this Court exercising revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.
